Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 76–77; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42 - Several cash flow lines print a dash or no line for some periods: amortization of gains on derivatives for fiscal 2024, fiscal 2025 and the 2026 half year; loss on extinguishment of debt for fiscal 2026 and both half years; acquisitions of HSA portfolios for both half years; settlement of derivatives for fiscal 2024, fiscal 2025 and the 2026 half year; proceeds from long-term debt and payment of debt issuance costs outside fiscal 2025; share repurchases in fiscal 2024. They are shown as not supplied, never as zero, and do not affect any total. Severity: Low. Action: none. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 91–92; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5 - The balance sheet shows no current portion of long-term debt and the debt note prints a dash for it, so Total Debt is long-term debt, net of issuance costs, and the current portion is shown as not supplied. Accumulated other comprehensive loss is a dash at the two earlier year ends and is shown as not supplied; the balance sheet shows no temporary equity line. Severity: Low. Action: none. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 106 - Carrying values are not printed by instrument, only in total; the debt note attributes the unamortized discount and issuance costs to the notes, but no carrying value for the notes is printed, so those costs are shown as one financing cost adjustment beside the principal of each instrument and senior secured and unsecured debt are stated at principal. Severity: Low. Action: none. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12 - The issuer is managed as one operating segment and discloses revenue by type (service, custodial and interchange) but no segment revenue, so no segment schedule is stated and no segment sum is made. Severity: Low. Action: none. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 93 - The cover page of the second quarter report shows about 0.19 million fewer shares outstanding at August 20, 2026 than the balance sheet at July 31, 2026, but the report states no repurchase or other event after the quarter end, so no pro forma net debt change is stated. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the subsequent period's cash flow or repurchase disclosure. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 2 - The maintenance and growth split of capital expenditure is not disclosed, so total capital expenditure is stated, and the issuer prints a rounding difference of one in fiscal 2026 depreciation and amortization between its reconciliation lines and its cash flow statement. Severity: Low. Action: none. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 91

facts.label: Ownership, group structure and financial policy
facts.text: HealthEquity is a listed Delaware company and no sponsor, parent or controlling holder is named in the supplied filings, so no sponsor fee, recapitalisation or exit channel is documented; holder percentages and director independence sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied. HealthEquity, Inc. is the borrower and the issuer of the notes, domestic subsidiaries guarantee both, and the revolver is secured on substantially all assets while the notes are unsecured, so the notes are effectively behind secured claims of up to USD 1.0 billion, of which USD 335.0 million is drawn. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is largely recurring and account-driven: service fees are fixed tiered fees paid monthly for the term of the client agreement, custodial revenue is yield on HSA cash and client-held funds, and interchange follows card spending and is the only transactional line at 15.27% of first-half revenue. Volume is rising, with HSAs up 8% and new HSAs from sales up 20% in the first half of fiscal 2027, while other benefit accounts fell 2%. Pricing power is mixed: the average yield on HSA cash rose from 3.51% to 3.83% as contracts repriced to higher yields, but average service fees per account and the average interchange rate both fell. Switching costs are high because accounts belong to the member and closure fees apply, retention is described as strong and no churn rate is disclosed. Revenue is therefore predictable in the service and custodial lines, rate-driven in custodial, regulated throughout because tax law creates the product, and not structurally declining. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Cost of revenue was 27.1% of revenue in the first half of fiscal 2027 against 30.4% a year earlier, because service costs fell 7% on technology efficiencies and lower fraud reimbursements, medical claims and consulting spend while revenue rose 7%; service gross margin rose by 7.41 percentage points to 38.76%. Custodial costs are small at 6.78% of custodial revenue, so custodial income reaches EBITDA almost in full. Operating expenses before amortization and integration rose 13.21% against revenue growth of 7.42%, led by technology and general and administrative spend, so part of the gross margin gain is being spent. Reported EBITDA margin was 39.98% in the first half against 38.06%. Stock-based compensation was 15.30% of fiscal 2026 reported EBITDA, which is why the issuer's adjusted EBITDA is 18.53% higher. Margins can be defended against volume pressure, but not against a custodial yield fall, because custodial costs are small and do not fall with the revenue, so the loss reaches EBITDA directly. facts.label: Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion
facts.text: Capital needs are small: capital expenditure was 10.61% of operating cash flow in fiscal 2026 and is expected to stay at the same level in fiscal 2027, mainly software. Free cash flow was 85.57% of reported EBITDA in fiscal 2026 and 85.75% over the last twelve months, but part of that is tax timing: deferred taxes of USD 28,340 thousand over the period were expense not paid in cash, and the company says the 2025 tax act accelerated deductions so that cash taxes in fiscal 2027 are expected to be significantly reduced, although first-half cash taxes were USD 35,586 thousand against USD 6,507 thousand a year earlier. After removing deferred taxes conversion is 80.19%. Costs of new accounts are incurred in the third and fourth quarters before the revenue arrives, so quarter-end leverage is seasonal. Free cash flow covers cash interest of USD 47,233 thousand over the last twelve months 9.25 times, which leaves room to service the debt and fund buybacks, and capital expenditure could be trimmed to protect cash, although the company plans to keep it level. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is intense and asymmetric: banks such as Optum Bank and Webster Bank and retail investment companies such as Fidelity Investments compete for HSAs with greater resources, and Fidelity has gained significant share, so competition can limit service pricing and obliges the company to offer competitive yields to keep members. New entrants need Treasury approval as a non-bank custodian or a bank charter, which has not stopped well-resourced entrants. Substitution comes from network partners that decide to offer HSAs directly, which the company says would reduce channel opportunities and cause attrition, and from policy change such as single payer proposals. Buyer power is moderate because no customer exceeds 10% of revenue and switching an HSA takes effort and may cost closure fees. Supplier power is the force that matters most for credit: insurance company and depository partners paid fees equal to about 48% of fiscal 2026 revenue and set the yield, one bank identification number sponsor supports the card programme, and one custodial investment partner holds invested balances, none of them named. facts.label: Policy, economic, social and technology factors
facts.text: Policy and economic factors are material to credit. HSA products exist because of tax law, the 2025 tax act widened HSA eligibility to Bronze and Catastrophic plans, and the company also says proposals to curtail HSAs or move to single payer could harm the business. Interest rates and equity markets set custodial yield and invested balances. Social and cost trends support demand: the company cites average family health insurance premiums up 26% since 2020, which increases cost sharing and HSA take-up. Technology matters through service-cost efficiency from technology investment and artificial intelligence tools, and through the 2024 cybersecurity incident whose litigation has no loss estimate. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are the company's stated expectation that yield on HSA cash rises further if rates hold, account growth with HSAs up 8%, wider HSA eligibility and continued service-cost efficiency; the headwinds are a possible fall in market rates, operating expenses growing faster than revenue, cash taxes that could rise towards the tax expense once accelerated deductions run off, which the filings do not schedule, and the open litigation. Over three to five years the maturity wall in 2029 and the policy environment for HSAs matter most: the whole USD 935.0 million falls due in fiscal 2030, and tax-law change can alter the product. The company gives no numeric guidance in the filings, so the direction rests on stated expectations and disclosed trends. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The downside is a falling-rate and falling-equity cycle. The first break is custodial revenue: new and repriced HSA cash earns less, client-held funds reprice immediately, and invested balances, now 54.20% of HSA Assets (calculation C24), fall in value and cut service fees. Because custodial costs are only 6.78% of custodial revenue, the loss reaches EBITDA almost in full; each 10% fall in custodial revenue removes USD 67,073.9 thousand, or 13.16% of EBITDA, and takes net leverage to 1.53x and cover to 9.37x with no cost saving. Free cash flow falls by a similar amount before tax while buybacks of USD 231,054 thousand in a half-year continue unless the board stops them, and the Treasury bond forwards settle in cash from August 2026 with a net liability of USD 85,198 thousand. Liquidity of USD 921,003 thousand before letters of credit and no maturity before fiscal 2030 mean there is no refinancing or liquidity event in the next two years; EBITDA would have to fall 43.39%, a custodial revenue fall of 32.96%, before leverage returned to the fiscal 2025 level. Management levers are suspending buybacks, trimming capital expenditure and the undrawn revolver, and resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; the observable triggers are the yield on repricing HSA cash, HSA cash growth, repurchases against free cash flow and the revolver balance. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, HealthEquity presents a strong business profile in scale and account stickiness, but credit quality is constrained by earnings concentrated in rate-linked custodial revenue and by buybacks that exceeded free cash flow in the latest half. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: free cash flow converts 85.57% of EBITDA, though 80.19% after deferred taxes. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage staying low and on the market in 2029, when the whole USD 935.0 million falls due. The primary downside path is lower rates and equity prices cutting custodial and fee income while buybacks continue. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the proxy statement, the yield on repricing cash, partner terms, a rating or price series and any later filing. Top risk: custodial income compression with buybacks funded from the revolver. ## Request

Source readiness for Healthequity, Inc. (issuer id hqy-1428336), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is whether the four supplied filings support the requested modules (Business & governance, Financial foundation and Fundamental credit) and what stays unsupported. The run settings state no other objective, so the objective is the pathway's use case, a credit snapshot.
## Sources

No output from another module is supplied to this module, which is the entry point of the run.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The supplied annual and quarterly filings support a credit snapshot of Healthequity, Inc. through the quarter ended July 31, 2026, with company-reported figures only; absent loan documents, ratings and market data mean covenant headroom, security terms and relative value cannot be tested here.

The four filings agree on every anchor figure cross-checked between them, and the latest report is 83 days old at the cutoff with no subsequent events disclosed. The gaps that matter to creditors are the absent credit agreement and indenture, which leave covenant definitions and guarantor names unverified; the absent report for the October 2025 quarter, which leaves the third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2026 available only as a combined half-year; and a cybersecurity litigation disclosure that narrowed across filings without explanation.

spans.text: # Financial foundation for Healthequity, Inc. (hqy-1428336), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Financial foundation for Healthequity, Inc. (issuer id hqy-1428336), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's income statement, cash flow statement, balance sheet, debt, liquidity and leverage and coverage metrics for fiscal 2024 to fiscal 2026 and the last twelve months to July 31, 2026, as printed in the four supplied filings. It builds no forecast and states no credit recommendation.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-01-31_hqy-20250131.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2025 | 2025-03-18 | 55111b8190b4fa9b93f90109e1da4cbdc89980381a4ad8595991b3f01ad19b55 | Balance sheet at January 31, 2024, the fiscal 2024 adjusted EBITDA reconciliation and the January 31, 2024 debt table and key metrics |

| 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026 | 2026-03-17 | 584215a6d4a1c670c61291e4837f3c609a40ec832ef88db837d7081d678d801f | Fiscal 2024 to 2026 income statement and cash flow statement, balance sheets at January 31, 2025 and 2026, debt note, contractual obligations table and adjusted EBITDA reconciliation |

| 10-Q_2026-04-30_hqy-20260430.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended April 30, 2026 | 2026-05-28 | 09ab82c0880caf050f33c0deb2e74342523834559e88e4182be439838f3232f2 | Cross-check of the January 31, 2026 balances that it reports again; no figure in the tables below is taken only from this report |

| Handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness | CP-0 | da6933a06816c56f8009b5d95355f213000fc9805a9e5f0892995e436bd1e613 | Confirmed the effective source set, the period labels, the absent report for the quarter ended October 31, 2025 and the absent loan documents |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Healthequity's reported net debt is 1.32x last-twelve-months EBITDA at July 31, 2026, and no debt falls due before fiscal 2030, so creditors face low leverage and little refinancing pressure; capital returns that outran free cash flow in the latest half-year are the pressure point.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 11–14; calculation C17; calculation C21; calculation C22

Net debt to reported EBITDA fell from 2.34x at fiscal 2025 to 1.34x at fiscal 2026 as EBITDA grew and USD 100 million of debt was repaid, and interest cover is 10.79x on the last twelve months. Reported EBITDA is calculated here because the issuer prints only an adjusted figure, on which net debt to EBITDA is 1.11x. Net debt rose by USD 36.61 million in the first half of fiscal 2027.
Basis: calculation C21; calculation C18; calculation C23; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Key findings

- Reported net debt to EBITDA fell from 2.34x at fiscal 2025 to 1.34x at fiscal 2026 and was 1.32x on a last-twelve-months basis at July 31, 2026, and total debt to EBITDA fell from 3.25x to 2.01x and 1.83x. Reported EBITDA grew by 46.83% in fiscal 2026 while total debt fell from USD 1,056.30 million to USD 957.38 million, so the fall in leverage comes from earnings growth and repayment together. On the issuer's adjusted EBITDA net leverage is 1.13x at fiscal 2026 and 1.11x at July 31, 2026, so the improvement does not depend on which EBITDA is chosen.
Basis: calculation C21; calculation C22; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 2

- EBITDA to cash interest paid rose from 5.55x at fiscal 2025 to 9.14x at fiscal 2026 and 10.79x on a last-twelve-months basis, because EBITDA grew and cash interest paid fell as debt was repaid; on adjusted EBITDA cover is 12.83x. The revolving credit facility floats, at 5.08% at July 31, 2026, while the 2029 notes are fixed, so only the revolver's USD 335 million of debt is exposed to a rise in rates.

- Free cash flow was 85.57% of reported EBITDA in fiscal 2026, but share repurchases absorbed 73.24% of it, and in the first half of fiscal 2027 repurchases were 114.60% of free cash flow, so net debt rose to USD 675.06 million at July 31, 2026 from USD 638.45 million at January 31, 2026 even though the revolver balance fell to USD 335 million. For creditors, equity returns now take more of the surplus cash than debt reduction does.
Basis: calculation C22; calculation C18; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 91

- Liquidity at July 31, 2026 is USD 256.00 million of cash plus USD 665 million undrawn on the revolving credit facility, before letters of credit, or USD 921.00 million in all, against USD 935 million of debt that falls due in fiscal 2030; no debt matures in fiscal 2027, 2028 or 2029, so the maturity wall is more than three years away.
Basis: calculation C19; calculation C20; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13

- Reported EBITDA is calculated here from the issuer's reconciliation lines, and the issuer's adjusted figure is 18.53% above it at fiscal 2026, mainly stock-based compensation, which creditors should treat as a real cost; neither is the covenant measure, so no covenant headroom is stated. Custodial revenue, which moves with interest rates, was 48.48% of fiscal 2026 revenue and 49.66% in the first half of fiscal 2027.
Basis: calculation C22; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 76–77; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 14
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

- Leverage is low and falling, but the earnings behind it are exposed to interest rates: custodial revenue was 49.66% of first-half revenue in fiscal 2027, and the issuer says a sustained decline in rates would reduce the yield and the custodial revenue it earns, although its contract structure mitigates the short-term effect. Cash taxes also rose to USD 35.59 million in the first half of fiscal 2027 from USD 6.51 million a year earlier, which weighs on free cash flow.
Basis: calculation C22; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 47

- The view would weaken if repurchases keep exceeding free cash flow and are funded from cash and the revolver, which would push net debt to EBITDA back toward the 2.34x of fiscal 2025, or if reported EBITDA falls with rates. It would strengthen if free cash flow again exceeds repurchases and the revolver is repaid.
Basis: calculation C21; calculation C22
### Limitations

- The report for the quarter ended October 31, 2025 is not supplied, so the third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2026 are not separately available; the last-twelve-months figures are built from the fiscal 2026 year and the two half years instead.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 90–92; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The amount of letters of credit outstanding is not stated, so undrawn capacity is shown before them, and the executed credit agreement is not supplied, so covenant definitions and reported covenant ratios are not established and no covenant headroom is stated.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; Source readiness (CP-0)
- Reported EBITDA is calculated here and interim ratios use last-twelve-months figures with no direct statement tie, so the interim ratio rests on the constructed period register.
### Chart data: leverage
| Period | Total debt / EBITDA | Net debt / EBITDA | Reporting unit | Basis and limitation |
| FY2024 / 2024-01-31 | 3.22 | 1.74 | x | Carrying-value debt over reported EBITDA calculated from the issuer's reconciliation lines; fiscal year row |
| FY2025 / 2025-01-31 | 3.25 | 2.34 | x | Carrying-value debt over reported EBITDA calculated from the issuer's reconciliation lines; fiscal year row |
| FY2026 / 2026-01-31 | 2.01 | 1.34 | x | Carrying-value debt over reported EBITDA calculated from the issuer's reconciliation lines; fiscal year row |
| 2026-07-31 | 1.83 | 1.32 | x | Carrying-value debt over last-twelve-months reported EBITDA built from fiscal 2026 plus the 2027 half year less the 2026 half year; interim row, no statement tie |
Reported EBITDA is the issuer's own pre-adjustment subtotal calculated here, not an issuer-printed figure and not the covenant measure.
### Chart data: interest cover

| FY2024 / 2024-01-31 | 5.48 | x | Reported EBITDA over cash interest paid in the cash flow statement; fiscal year row |

Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12

- The issuer is managed as one operating segment and discloses revenue by type (service, custodial and interchange) but no segment revenue, so no segment schedule is stated and no segment sum is made. Severity: Low. Action: none.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 93

- The cover page of the second quarter report shows about 0.19 million fewer shares outstanding at August 20, 2026 than the balance sheet at July 31, 2026, but the report states no repurchase or other event after the quarter end, so no pro forma net debt change is stated. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the subsequent period's cash flow or repurchase disclosure.

- The maintenance and growth split of capital expenditure is not disclosed, so total capital expenditure is stated, and the issuer prints a rounding difference of one in fiscal 2026 depreciation and amortization between its reconciliation lines and its cash flow statement. Severity: Low. Action: none.

spans.text: # Business & governance for Healthequity, Inc. (hqy-1428336), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Business & governance for Healthequity, Inc. (issuer id hqy-1428336), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, history, financial-policy behaviour and sponsor and governance risk that matter to creditors, taken from the four supplied filings and the source readiness findings. It states no credit recommendation, rating, recovery view or inference about sponsor willingness.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-01-31_hqy-20250131.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2025 | 2025-03-18 | 55111b8190b4fa9b93f90109e1da4cbdc89980381a4ad8595991b3f01ad19b55 | Business description at 2025-01-31, the BenefitWallet tranche table, the HealthSavings purchase, the chief executive transition and the first description of the cybersecurity litigation |

| Handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness | CP-0 | da6933a06816c56f8009b5d95355f213000fc9805a9e5f0892995e436bd1e613 | Confirmed the effective source set, the absent proxy statement, executed loan documents, releases and later filings, and the narrowed litigation wording |
## Findings
### Bottom line

HealthEquity is a scaled, listed HSA custodian with no sponsor or controlling holder named, so creditors face little ownership-driven extraction risk, but nearly half of revenue and most gross profit come from interest-linked custodial fees, and latest-half buybacks exceeded free cash flow.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 122; calculation C5; calculation C8; calculation C11

The franchise is large, with HSA Assets of USD 37.9 billion at July 31, 2026, and no customer provides more than 10% of revenue. The board added USD 1.0 billion to the repurchase authorization in May 2026, and first-half repurchases were 114.60% of free cash flow while cash fell. Sponsor and governance risk is Medium: it would rise if buybacks were funded from the revolver and fall if the proxy statement confirms independent oversight.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-04-30_hqy-20260430.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C11; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

- The business is a recurring-fee franchise rather than a transaction-driven one, which supports revenue visibility. The company holds HSA Assets of USD 37.9 billion for its members, reports about 20% of the HSA market by assets, says most accounts open before each fiscal year starts, and has no customer above 10% of revenue. The market share figure is a company statement citing an industry report.

- Earnings depend on interest rates and a small set of partners. Custodial revenue is 49.66% of first-half revenue and 63.49% of gross profit, and fees from insurance company and depository partners were about 48% of fiscal 2026 revenue, up from 39% in fiscal 2024. USD 2.3 billion of HSA cash earning 1.5% reprices in the rest of fiscal 2027, against a book average of 3.9%, so custodial income follows the rates at which cash reprices.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C5; calculation C8; calculation C23

- Asset growth is coming from invested balances, not cash, which makes fee income market-sensitive. HSA investments are 54.20% of HSA Assets against 45.70% at January 31, 2025, and grew 28% in the year to July 31, 2026 while HSA cash grew 2%. Invested balances earn fees set as a percentage of the balance, so a market fall would cut service fees while the cash that earns custodial revenue is nearly flat.

- No sponsor, parent or controlling holder appears in the supplied filings, so there is no documented sponsor fee, dividend recapitalisation or exit channel, and the company has no current plans to pay dividends. The company reports 19 holders of record, not counting holders in street name, the percentage held by any holder is not stated, and ownership, director independence and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so low extraction risk rests on absence of disclosure.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 1; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Financial policy has moved from returns funded by free cash flow to returns above it, a mixed rather than extractive pattern. Repurchases were 73.24% of free cash flow in fiscal 2026 and 114.60% in the first half of fiscal 2027, USD 948.4 million of authorization remains, which is 2.17x last-twelve-months free cash flow, and cash fell and net debt rose in the half. The revolver was still reduced, no borrowing is described for buybacks and no dividend is paid.

Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C11; calculation C14; calculation C16

- Acquisitions have been portfolio purchases paid partly with borrowings, and leverage has been brought back but not to its starting point. The USD 425.0 million BenefitWallet purchase in 2024 was paid with USD 225.0 million of revolver borrowings and USD 200.0 million of cash; revolver principal is now 27.47% below its January 31, 2025 level, yet total debt principal is 5.43% above its level at January 31, 2024, before the purchase, and integration expense has largely run off. The revolver is described as available for acquisitions, and the company calls acquisitions a selective strategy, which is management language.

Basis: 10-K_2025-01-31_hqy-20250131.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-K_2025-01-31_hqy-20250131.htm.jsonl, page 105; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C26

- Audit and reporting quality are adequate for creditor monitoring, with one open item. The auditor stated that the statements present fairly and that internal control was effective, the chair is separate from the chief executive, and a board committee oversees cybersecurity. The cybersecurity litigation has no loss estimate or accrual and its description narrowed between the 2025 and 2026 annual reports without explanation, so that exposure is unquantified.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a low-risk reading is that capital return has outrun cash generation. First-half repurchases were 114.60% of free cash flow, the new authorization is 2.17x last-twelve-months free cash flow, and the revolver that funded the 2024 acquisition is also the stated source for further acquisitions. The view would move to High if repurchases were funded by revolver draws, if a dividend were introduced, or if the credit agreement proved to allow wide distributions.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C11; calculation C14

The Medium level also rests on facts that could improve. The proxy statement could confirm independent directors, no related-party dealings and no large holder, and the cybersecurity case could be dismissed or capped. Partner dependence is a business risk rather than a governance one, but no partner is named and no single-partner share is stated, so a loss of a large partner would change the custodial view and cannot be tested here.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so holder percentages, director independence, committee membership, related-party dealings and executive pay are not stated; the low-extraction reading of ownership, the governance conclusions and the Medium level rest on the annual report's cover, signature pages and exhibit list alone, and a large holder or related-party dealing would raise the level.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 126; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The executed credit agreement is not supplied, so room for distributions, investments and new debt is not stated; the mixed reading of buybacks and acquisitions is judged from cash generation alone, with capacity kept separate from willingness, and wide baskets would make it less comfortable.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 108–109; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Nothing after the quarterly report signed on August 27, 2026 is supplied, so repurchases, acquisitions or financing since then are not established; the buyback pace behind the Medium level is observed only to the end of July 2026 and a faster pace would change it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 50; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The market share and ranking figures come from an industry report that the company cites and that is not supplied, so the view that the franchise is strong rests on the company's own statements for that point.

- The cybersecurity litigation carries no loss estimate and the reason its description narrowed is not stated, so the conclusion that reporting quality is adequate treats that exposure as open and could change if a loss is estimated.
### Company and operating model
| Item | Detail | Source |

| Business | Technology-enabled administrator of consumer health savings accounts (HSAs) and other consumer-directed benefits (flexible spending accounts, health reimbursement arrangements, COBRA and commuter benefits), managed as one operating segment | 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 93 |

| How it earns revenue | Service fees from clients, network partners and members; custodial revenue on HSA cash held by insurance company partners and depository partners; interchange fees on card spending | 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 30 |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No acquisition, sponsor transaction or new debt issue is pending or described in the supplied filings after the quarter ended July 31, 2026, and the run settings name no transaction, so this section records the completed transactions that shape the creditor position. The latest debt financing is the five-year senior secured revolving credit facility of up to USD 1.0 billion entered on August 23, 2024, which refinanced the prior credit agreement, the facility under which the BenefitWallet purchase had been funded. USD 335.0 million is drawn at July 31, 2026, alongside USD 600 million of 4.50% senior notes due 2029 issued in October 2021.

The BenefitWallet HSA portfolio, bought for USD 425.0 million with USD 2.7 billion of HSA Assets, closed in three tranches between March and May 2024 and was paid with USD 225.0 million of revolver borrowings and USD 200.0 million of cash. The board has since raised the repurchase authorization twice, in June 2025 and May 2026, to USD 1.6 billion in all, and the filings describe no borrowing to fund repurchases.

- The depository partner contract assumed with BenefitWallet was due to expire in June 2026 and no later filing states the outcome. Severity: Low. Action: check the next quarterly report.
Basis: 10-K_2025-01-31_hqy-20250131.htm.jsonl, page 101

- Partner names (insurance company, depository, investment and card sponsor) and the share of revenue from any one partner are not stated, so concentration is known only in aggregate. Severity: Medium. Action: request partner concentration data from the issuer.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C23

- Two repurchase figures exist for each period and the authorization used differs slightly from repurchases recorded, which is shown in the conflict log and does not change the conclusions. Severity: Low. Action: none beyond the labelled comparison.

spans.text: # Fundamental credit for Healthequity, Inc. (hqy-1428336), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Fundamental credit for Healthequity, Inc. (issuer id hqy-1428336), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the integrated fundamental credit view built on the source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance findings and the four supplied filings. It states no security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion, formal rating or portfolio sizing.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

## Findings
### Bottom line

HealthEquity is a low-leverage credit with no debt due before fiscal 2030, so creditors face little near-term risk, but earnings tied to interest rates and buybacks that exceeded free cash flow in the latest half are the pressure points.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C1; calculation C9; calculation C17

Reported net debt is 1.32x last-twelve-months EBITDA and interest cover is 10.79x. Custodial revenue, which follows interest rates, supplies 63.49% of gross profit, so a 10% fall in it with no cost saving would remove 13.16% of EBITDA. The view would weaken if buybacks were funded from the revolver and strengthen if free cash flow again exceeds them.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C7; calculation C9; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Key findings

- The strongest support is balance sheet capacity: net debt is 1.32x reported EBITDA and cover is 10.79x, so at today's net debt earnings could fall by 43.39% before leverage returned to the 2.34x of fiscal 2025. No debt matures before fiscal 2030, and USD 665.0 million of the revolver is undrawn before letters of credit alongside USD 256.0 million of cash, so there is no refinancing need or liquidity squeeze in the next two years.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C8; calculation C13; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Cash generation is solid but flattered by tax timing. Free cash flow was 85.57% of reported EBITDA in fiscal 2026 and capital expenditure took 10.61% of operating cash flow, yet deferred taxes meant that part of the tax expense was not paid in cash, and free cash flow after deferred taxes is 80.19% of EBITDA, so durable conversion is nearer four fifths than the headline.

Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 91–92; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- The weakest dimension is earnings concentration in rate-linked custodial revenue, which is 49.66% of first-half revenue and 63.49% of gross profit at a 93.22% gross margin, with partners that hold the cash paying fees equal to about 48% of fiscal 2026 revenue. A fall of 43.39% in EBITDA, equal to 32.96% of custodial revenue with no cost saving, would be needed to return net leverage to the fiscal 2025 level, so the exposure is large in earnings terms but far from distressing leverage.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C8; calculation C9; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- The franchise supports revenue visibility but not pricing power. HSAs grew 8% in the year to July 31, 2026, accounts belong to members and carry closure fees, and retention is described as strong, while average service fees per account and the average card interchange rate both fell, and the yield on HSA cash rose 32 bp to 3.83% as lower-yield contracts repriced. Volume, not price, drives growth outside custodial yield.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C20

- Financial policy is the second constraint and is mixed rather than adverse. Repurchases were 73.24% of free cash flow in fiscal 2026 and 114.60% in the first half of fiscal 2027, USD 948.4 million of authorization remains, which is 2.17x last-twelve-months free cash flow, and net debt rose while the revolver was still reduced. The board can stop repurchases at any time, which is the main management lever, and sponsor and governance risk is Medium on the earlier assessment.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C22; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Refinancing is a single-year question. The whole USD 935.0 million of principal falls due in fiscal 2030, with the revolver and the notes 39 days apart, and the notes are redeemable at par since October 1, 2026; their fair value is 97.17% of principal, a Level 2 estimate. No rating or market price series is supplied, so market access is judged from the maturity profile and low leverage alone, and the issue becomes live in fiscal 2029.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 107; calculation C14; calculation C15; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The primary downside path runs from lower interest rates and equity prices to custodial and investment-fee income, and the monitor is the yield on repricing HSA cash against the 3.9% book average. Treasury bond forwards hedge part of future placements but carry a net liability of USD 85,198 thousand, 9.25% of liquidity, so the hedge is a liability today and becomes protection only if rates fall.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C13; calculation C16
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a comfortable reading is the mix of earnings and capital return: custodial revenue supplies 63.49% of gross profit, first-half repurchases were 114.60% of free cash flow, and cash taxes in fiscal 2026 were low through accelerated deductions, so reported free cash flow may overstate what recurs. The view would weaken if repurchases were funded from the revolver, if the yield on repricing HSA cash fell below the book average, or if the litigation produced a material loss.

Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C5; calculation C9; calculation C17

The evidence for a better outcome is that the company states it expects its yield on HSA cash to rise further if rates stay where they are, service costs fell 7% while service revenue rose 4%, and a 10% fall in custodial revenue would still leave net leverage at 1.53x and cover at 9.37x. The view would strengthen if free cash flow again exceeds repurchases, the revolver is repaid further and the credit agreement shows narrow distribution baskets.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C7; calculation C10
### Limitations

- The filings do not disclose the yield at which maturing HSA cash will reprice or the contract terms with each partner, so the size and timing of any custodial income effect of a rate move cannot be computed and the downside is a static sensitivity on revenue, not a forecast.

- The filings give only qualitative expectations and no numeric guidance, earnings release or investor presentation, so the outlook is the analyst's reading of disclosed trends and company statements and may differ from the company's own expectations.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 34; Source readiness (CP-0)

- No agency rating and no traded price are supplied beyond the notes' fair value estimate, so the conclusion that refinancing capacity is sound rests on the maturity profile and leverage and has not been tested against market access.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 20; Source readiness (CP-0)
- The cash-tax benefit from accelerated deductions is not scheduled in the filings, so the share of free cash flow that will recur is estimated from deferred taxes and could be lower or higher.
### Strengths and weaknesses

- Strength: low leverage and long-dated debt. Net debt is 1.32x EBITDA and cover is 10.79x, which lets earnings absorb a large fall before leverage reaches the fiscal 2025 level, and no principal is due until fiscal 2030, so default risk from refinancing or liquidity is low for the next two years.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C8; calculation C14; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Strength: sticky, member-owned accounts with low capital needs. HSAs belong to members and carry closure fees, retention is strong on the company's account, and capital expenditure took 10.61% of operating cash flow, so account growth converts to cash that services debt.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C6

- Strength: cost efficiency in the service line. Service costs fell 7% while service revenue rose 4%, lifting service gross margin by 7.41 percentage points, which cushions the margin if revenue growth slows.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C10

- Weakness: earnings concentration in rate-linked custodial revenue. It is 63.49% of gross profit, partners paying the yield supply about 48% of revenue, and each 10% fall removes 13.16% of EBITDA, so a falling-rate cycle would hit the largest profit pool first.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C7; calculation C9

- Weakness: capital return above cash generation. Repurchases were 114.60% of free cash flow in the first half, authorization remaining is 2.17x last-twelve-months free cash flow, and the revolver is the funding backstop, so leverage can rise without any earnings fall.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C17; calculation C18

- Weakness: a single maturity year and floating-rate revolver. All principal falls due within 39 days in 2029, and the revolver floats at 5.08%, so a closed market in 2029 would hit the whole stack at once, although a one percent rate rise costs only about USD 3.4 million a year.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C14; calculation C21

### Company description and credit linkage

HealthEquity administers consumer health savings accounts and other consumer-directed benefits and earns service fees, custodial yield on HSA cash and card interchange. Its credit relevance is that most accounts are opened before each fiscal year begins, which gives revenue visibility, while custodial yield makes about half of revenue sensitive to interest rates. At July 31, 2026 it held 10,739 thousand HSAs with USD 37.9 billion of HSA Assets, HSAs grew 8% in the year, and it describes itself as the largest provider by accounts and second by assets, citing an industry report. It is one operating segment with no customer above 10% of revenue, which limits single-customer loss but not the reliance on a few insurance and bank partners that hold the cash and set the yield.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 84; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Ownership, group structure and financial policy

HealthEquity is a listed Delaware company and no sponsor, parent or controlling holder is named in the supplied filings, so no sponsor fee, recapitalisation or exit channel is documented; holder percentages and director independence sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied. HealthEquity, Inc. is the borrower and the issuer of the notes, domestic subsidiaries guarantee both, and the revolver is secured on substantially all assets while the notes are unsecured, so the notes are effectively behind secured claims of up to USD 1.0 billion, of which USD 335.0 million is drawn. Financial policy is mixed: there is no dividend and revolver prepayments were USD 100.0 million in fiscal 2026, but repurchases ran above free cash flow in the latest half and the authorization was raised by USD 1.0 billion in May 2026. This view adopts the Medium sponsor and governance level from Business & governance; capacity to distribute under the credit agreement is not established.

Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 107–109; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 80; Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is largely recurring and account-driven: service fees are fixed tiered fees paid monthly for the term of the client agreement, custodial revenue is yield on HSA cash and client-held funds, and interchange follows card spending and is the only transactional line at 15.27% of first-half revenue. Volume is rising, with HSAs up 8% and new HSAs from sales up 20% in the first half of fiscal 2027, while other benefit accounts fell 2%. Pricing power is mixed: the average yield on HSA cash rose from 3.51% to 3.83% as contracts repriced to higher yields, but average service fees per account and the average interchange rate both fell. Switching costs are high because accounts belong to the member and closure fees apply, retention is described as strong and no churn rate is disclosed. Revenue is therefore predictable in the service and custodial lines, rate-driven in custodial, regulated throughout because tax law creates the product, and not structurally declining.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C20; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Cost of revenue was 27.1% of revenue in the first half of fiscal 2027 against 30.4% a year earlier, because service costs fell 7% on technology efficiencies and lower fraud reimbursements, medical claims and consulting spend while revenue rose 7%; service gross margin rose by 7.41 percentage points to 38.76%. Custodial costs are small at 6.78% of custodial revenue, so custodial income reaches EBITDA almost in full. Operating expenses before amortization and integration rose 13.21% against revenue growth of 7.42%, led by technology and general and administrative spend, so part of the gross margin gain is being spent. Reported EBITDA margin was 39.98% in the first half against 38.06%. Stock-based compensation was 15.30% of fiscal 2026 reported EBITDA, which is why the issuer's adjusted EBITDA is 18.53% higher. Margins can be defended against volume pressure, but not against a custodial yield fall, because custodial costs are small and do not fall with the revenue, so the loss reaches EBITDA directly.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 36–37; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 91; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C19; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion

Capital needs are small: capital expenditure was 10.61% of operating cash flow in fiscal 2026 and is expected to stay at the same level in fiscal 2027, mainly software. Free cash flow was 85.57% of reported EBITDA in fiscal 2026 and 85.75% over the last twelve months, but part of that is tax timing: deferred taxes of USD 28,340 thousand over the period were expense not paid in cash, and the company says the 2025 tax act accelerated deductions so that cash taxes in fiscal 2027 are expected to be significantly reduced, although first-half cash taxes were USD 35,586 thousand against USD 6,507 thousand a year earlier. After removing deferred taxes conversion is 80.19%. Costs of new accounts are incurred in the third and fourth quarters before the revenue arrives, so quarter-end leverage is seasonal. Free cash flow covers cash interest of USD 47,233 thousand over the last twelve months 9.25 times, which leaves room to service the debt and fund buybacks, and capital expenditure could be trimmed to protect cash, although the company plans to keep it level.

Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C25; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense and asymmetric: banks such as Optum Bank and Webster Bank and retail investment companies such as Fidelity Investments compete for HSAs with greater resources, and Fidelity has gained significant share, so competition can limit service pricing and obliges the company to offer competitive yields to keep members. New entrants need Treasury approval as a non-bank custodian or a bank charter, which has not stopped well-resourced entrants. Substitution comes from network partners that decide to offer HSAs directly, which the company says would reduce channel opportunities and cause attrition, and from policy change such as single payer proposals. Buyer power is moderate because no customer exceeds 10% of revenue and switching an HSA takes effort and may cost closure fees. Supplier power is the force that matters most for credit: insurance company and depository partners paid fees equal to about 48% of fiscal 2026 revenue and set the yield, one bank identification number sponsor supports the card programme, and one custodial investment partner holds invested balances, none of them named.
### Policy, economic, social and technology factors

Policy and economic factors are material to credit. HSA products exist because of tax law, the 2025 tax act widened HSA eligibility to Bronze and Catastrophic plans, and the company also says proposals to curtail HSAs or move to single payer could harm the business. Interest rates and equity markets set custodial yield and invested balances. Social and cost trends support demand: the company cites average family health insurance premiums up 26% since 2020, which increases cost sharing and HSA take-up. Technology matters through service-cost efficiency from technology investment and artificial intelligence tools, and through the 2024 cybersecurity incident whose litigation has no loss estimate.
### Credit-translated SWOT
- Strengths: low leverage and long-dated debt; sticky member-owned accounts; low capital needs; service-cost efficiency; a USD 1.0 billion revolver with USD 665.0 million undrawn.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C6; calculation C10; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 13

- Weaknesses: custodial revenue concentration in rate-linked earnings; reliance on a few partners; capital return above free cash flow in the latest half; all principal due in one fiscal year; litigation with no loss estimate.
Basis: calculation C9; calculation C14; calculation C17; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11

- Opportunities that could improve credit quality: repricing of low-yield HSA cash to current yields, wider HSA eligibility under the 2025 tax act, further service-cost efficiency, and refinancing early at par since the notes became redeemable at par on October 1, 2026.

- Threats that could weaken credit quality: a sustained fall in market rates or equity prices, network partners offering HSAs directly, policy change against HSAs, loss of a large partner, and a revolver-funded buyback or acquisition.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C7
### Financial profile and credit quality

The main supports are low leverage (1.32x net debt to EBITDA), high cover (10.79x), no maturity before fiscal 2030, liquidity of USD 921,003 thousand before letters of credit and sticky accounts. The constraints are concentration of profit in rate-linked custodial revenue, buybacks above free cash flow in the latest half, a single maturity year and unverified governance facts. The trend is favourable: net leverage fell from 2.34x at fiscal 2025 to 1.34x at fiscal 2026 and 1.32x at the last twelve months, but net debt rose by USD 36,607 thousand in the first half of fiscal 2027. Missing datapoints are covenant definitions and reported covenant ratios, the letters of credit outstanding, the yield at which maturing cash will reprice, partner names and terms, the proxy statement and any rating or market price.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C13; calculation C22; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are the company's stated expectation that yield on HSA cash rises further if rates hold, account growth with HSAs up 8%, wider HSA eligibility and continued service-cost efficiency; the headwinds are a possible fall in market rates, operating expenses growing faster than revenue, cash taxes that could rise towards the tax expense once accelerated deductions run off, which the filings do not schedule, and the open litigation. Over three to five years the maturity wall in 2029 and the policy environment for HSAs matter most: the whole USD 935.0 million falls due in fiscal 2030, and tax-law change can alter the product. The company gives no numeric guidance in the filings, so the direction rests on stated expectations and disclosed trends.

### Downside scenario

The downside is a falling-rate and falling-equity cycle. The first break is custodial revenue: new and repriced HSA cash earns less, client-held funds reprice immediately, and invested balances, now 54.20% of HSA Assets (calculation C24), fall in value and cut service fees. Because custodial costs are only 6.78% of custodial revenue, the loss reaches EBITDA almost in full; each 10% fall in custodial revenue removes USD 67,073.9 thousand, or 13.16% of EBITDA, and takes net leverage to 1.53x and cover to 9.37x with no cost saving. Free cash flow falls by a similar amount before tax while buybacks of USD 231,054 thousand in a half-year continue unless the board stops them, and the Treasury bond forwards settle in cash from August 2026 with a net liability of USD 85,198 thousand. Liquidity of USD 921,003 thousand before letters of credit and no maturity before fiscal 2030 mean there is no refinancing or liquidity event in the next two years; EBITDA would have to fall 43.39%, a custodial revenue fall of 32.96%, before leverage returned to the fiscal 2025 level. Management levers are suspending buybacks, trimming capital expenditure and the undrawn revolver, and resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; the observable triggers are the yield on repricing HSA cash, HSA cash growth, repurchases against free cash flow and the revolver balance.

### Overall credit view

Overall, HealthEquity presents a strong business profile in scale and account stickiness, but credit quality is constrained by earnings concentrated in rate-linked custodial revenue and by buybacks that exceeded free cash flow in the latest half. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: free cash flow converts 85.57% of EBITDA, though 80.19% after deferred taxes. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage staying low and on the market in 2029, when the whole USD 935.0 million falls due. The primary downside path is lower rates and equity prices cutting custodial and fee income while buybacks continue. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the proxy statement, the yield on repricing cash, partner terms, a rating or price series and any later filing. Top risk: custodial income compression with buybacks funded from the revolver.
